title: Total quotient ring as a product over minimal primes
statement: Let A be a commutative ring [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with finitely many minimal prime ideals q_1, ..., q_t. Suppose every weakly associated prime of A (a prime ideal minimal among the prime ideals containing the annihilator of some element of A) is one of the q_i. Let S be the multiplicative set of non-zero-divisors of A and Q(A)=S^{-1}A [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Then the canonical map Q(A) \to A_{q_1} \times \cdots \times A_{q_t}, sending a fraction to its images in the localizations at the q_i [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], is an isomorphism.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.25.4, tag 02LX (lemma-total-ring-fractions-no-embedded-points), total quotient ring decomposition; its zerodivisor hypothesis is supplied by Algebra, Lemma 10.66.7, tag 05C3 (lemma-weakly-ass-zero-divisors), with Definition 10.66.1, tag 0547

proof.text: If x is a zero-divisor, choose y ≠ 0 with xy = 0. The annihilator I = (0 : y) is proper because 1 in I would give y = 0. By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-over-proper-ideal], choose r minimal over I. The hypothesis hweak makes r a minimal prime of A, and x belongs to r because I ≤ r. Conversely, [lem-pc-minimal-prime-avoids-nonzerodivisor] makes every minimal prime disjoint from the non-zero-divisors. Thus the zero-divisors are exactly the union of the listed minimal primes. Only the elementary forward direction of the weak-association union theorem is needed.

Use the localization prime correspondence of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] (Mathlib IsLocalization.primeSpectrumOrderIso). A prime disjoint from non-zero-divisors lies in the finite union of minimal primes by Step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] it is contained in one of them; minimality forces equality. Conversely every minimal prime is disjoint from the denominators. This constructs an equivalence E from Spec Q(A) to the minimal primes of A, and e = q composed with E inverse enumerates Spec Q(A).

The enumeration e proves Spec Q(A) finite. Every prime p of Q(A) lies in a maximal ideal m. The contractions of p and m to A are minimal primes by Step 2, so their inclusion is equality. Injectivity of contraction for localization gives p = m. Hence Q(A) has Krull dimension at most zero. Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.discreteTopology_iff_finite_and_krullDimLE_zero gives a discrete spectrum, and PrimeSpectrum.toPiLocalizationEquiv, the prime-spectrum version of [lem-weil-pbc-product-of-localizations-at-maximal], gives Q(A) ≃ₐ[Q(A)] ∏ P, Q(A)_P. Restrict scalars to A.

For P = e(i), the contraction equality E(E inverse(q(i))) = q(i) identifies its contraction with q(i). Part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] makes Q(A)_P a localization of A at q(i). Uniqueness of localization (IsLocalization.algEquiv) gives Q(A)_P ≃ₐ[A] A_{q(i)}. Reindex the product with AlgEquiv.piCongrLeft and apply these equivalences with AlgEquiv.piCongrRight. Composing with Step 3 gives the requested A-algebra equivalence. Every map fixes A, so the resulting map is the canonical fraction map. These equivalences and finite-spectrum results also apply when t = 0.

lean.statement: theorem totalQuotientRing_isProduct_minimalPrimes {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {t : ℕ} (q : Fin t ≃ {p : PrimeSpectrum A // p.asIdeal ∈ minimalPrimes A}) (hweak : ∀ (a : A) (p : Ideal A), p ∈ ((⊥ : Submodule A A).colon {a}).minimalPrimes → p ∈ minimalPrimes A) : Nonempty (Localization (nonZeroDivisors A) ≃ₐ[A] (∀ i : Fin t, Localization.AtPrime (q i).val.asIdeal))
